title: Mediterranean Tuna and White Bean Pita Pockets
intro: Mashing white beans into tuna provides lean protein and steady carbohydrates to keep you full well into the afternoon. Skipping traditional mayonnaise keeps saturated fat low while letting the bright flavors of lemon and fresh vegetables shine.

ingredients.name: no-salt-added canned chunk light tuna in water
ingredients.canonical_name: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, without salt, drained solids

ingredients.name: no-salt-added canned cannellini beans
ingredients.canonical_name: Beans, white, mature seeds, canned, no salt added

ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes
ingredients.canonical_name: Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average

instructions: Place the drained cannellini beans in a medium mixing bowl and mash with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving a few chunks for texture.
Add the drained tuna to the bowl with the mashed beans. Pour in the olive oil and lemon juice, sprinkle with black pepper, and mix thoroughly.
Fold the chopped parsley, red onion, cucumber, and cherry tomatoes into the tuna mixture until evenly combined.
Cut the whole-wheat pitas in half to create pockets and pry each one open.
Spoon the filling into the pita pockets and serve immediately.
variation: Swap the canned tuna for flaked, untreated canned pink salmon.
conservation: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; assemble in fresh pitas just before serving.
validation_warnings: Stage 4 qualifier: 'no-salt-added canned cannellini beans': the recipe uses a canned product but the match is cooked from dry (different water content, so a different weight basis). No candidate in the USDA shortlist satisfies it, so [175203] Beans, white, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt was kept — treat this ingredient's contribution as an over-statement.

Stage 4 coverage: 'extra-virgin olive oil': [748608] Oil, olive, extra virgin has no USDA value for fiber_g, protein_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [171413] Oil, olive, salad or cooking.
